title: Add a Postgres adapter for PlanStore
body:
`packages/core/src/ports.ts` defines `PlanStore`; only the in-memory adapter exists.

Add a Postgres implementation in a new `packages/store-postgres` package, plus the `plans` table migration. Amounts are stored as `NUMERIC(23,7)` or as a stroop `BIGINT` — pick one, say why in the PR, and keep it consistent with ADR 0003.

**Acceptance:** the existing in-memory `PlanStore` tests run green against the Postgres adapter via a shared test suite.

title: Add a Postgres adapter for SubscriptionStore
body:
Implement `SubscriptionStore` against Postgres, including `due(at)`.

`due()` must return only subscriptions whose `current_period_end <= at` **and** whose `next_attempt_at` is null or past. Index accordingly — this query runs every tick.

**Acceptance:** shared store suite passes; `EXPLAIN` shows an index scan, not a sequential scan, on a table of 100k subscriptions.

title: Add a Postgres adapter for InvoiceStore with a uniqueness guarantee
body:
Implement `InvoiceStore` on Postgres. Add a unique index on `(subscription_id, period_start)` so that double-billing a period is impossible at the database level, not only through `findByPeriod`.

**Acceptance:** a test that races two concurrent `create` calls for the same period ends with exactly one invoice and one caught constraint violation.

title: Add Postgres adapters for EventStore and WebhookStore
body:
Implement the remaining two ports. Events are append-only and read newest-first with a limit; webhook secrets must be stored hashed or encrypted at rest, never in plaintext.

**Acceptance:** shared store suite passes; a webhook row read straight from SQL does not reveal a usable signing secret.

title: Write the initial SQL migrations and a migration runner
body:
Pick a migration tool (or ~80 lines of runner — argue for whichever on the issue), add `migrations/0001_init.sql` covering plans, subscriptions, invoices, events, webhook_endpoints.

**Acceptance:** `pnpm migrate` brings an empty database to current, is idempotent, and runs in CI against the compose Postgres.

title: Run the store test suite against both adapters in CI
body:
Extract the in-memory store tests into a shared conformance suite parameterised by adapter factory, and run it against both in-memory and Postgres in CI.

**Acceptance:** one suite, two adapters, both green; a behavioural difference between adapters fails the build.

title: Lock due subscriptions with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
body:
Two scheduler instances against one database currently double-charge. Make `due()` claim rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` inside the tick's transaction.

**Acceptance:** a test that runs two concurrent `runBillingCycle` calls against the same Postgres charges each subscription exactly once.

title: Support a configurable page size and cursor on list endpoints
body:
`GET /v1/plans`, `/v1/events` and the invoice list return everything. Add opaque cursor pagination (`?limit=&starting_after=`) through the store ports so it works for both adapters.

**Acceptance:** documented in the README API table; tests cover first page, middle page, and an invalid cursor.

title: Persist the ledger instead of holding it in memory
body:
`packages/ledger` keeps entries in an array, so the audit trail dies with the process. Add a `LedgerStore` port and a Postgres adapter; keep the balance assertion on write.

**Acceptance:** entries survive a restart; `balance()` is a SQL aggregate, not a full scan in JS.

title: Reject an unbalanced entry before any partial write
body:
Once the ledger is persisted, `assertBalanced` must run before the transaction opens, not after the first insert.

**Acceptance:** a test proves a rejected entry leaves zero rows behind.

title: Add a reconciliation report: ledger vs invoices
body:
Add `pnpm reconcile` that reports, per merchant: invoices marked paid with no settling ledger entry, ledger settlements with no paid invoice, and any account whose receivable balance is non-zero for more than one period.

**Acceptance:** the command exits non-zero when it finds a discrepancy, so it can run in cron.

title: Exercise the SEP-41 executor against Stellar testnet end to end
body:
`SorobanAllowanceExecutor` is written but has never touched a network. Write a scripted testnet run: fund two accounts, `approve` an allowance, charge three monthly periods with a fast clock, and print the transaction hashes.

**Acceptance:** `scripts/testnet-e2e.ts` runs from a clean testnet, and the resulting transaction hashes go in the README.

title: Verify allowance before charging and skip a charge that cannot succeed
body:
The engine submits a `transfer_from` that simulation will reject when the allowance is short. Call `executor.allowance()` first and fail fast with `insufficient_allowance`, saving the simulation round trip.

**Acceptance:** `MockExecutor`-backed test shows no charge attempted when the allowance is below the plan amount.

title: Classify contract errors from structured diagnostics, not message text
body:
`classify()` in `soroban-executor.ts` string-matches error messages, which will silently mis-classify when the SDK changes wording. Parse the simulation error's diagnostic events / contract error codes instead, and keep the text match only as a last resort.

**Acceptance:** unit tests use recorded RPC error payloads rather than hand-written strings.

title: Warn merchants when a payer's allowance is running low
body:
A payer whose allowance covers fewer than two more periods will fail soon. Add a check on each successful charge and emit a new `subscription.allowance_low` event.

**Acceptance:** event type added to the schema, webhook docs, and covered by a test.

title: Add a Horizon classic-payment executor for non-Soroban assets
body:
Not every asset is wrapped as a SEP-41 contract. Add a second `PaymentExecutor` for classic payments where the payer has pre-signed a payment (documented limitations and all), behind the same interface.

**Acceptance:** the engine works with either executor with no change to the scheduler; ADR added explaining the trade-off.

title: Handle a transaction that times out but later succeeds
body:
`confirm()` returns `timeout` after 30s; the transaction can still land afterwards, and the retry would double-charge. Record the submitted transaction hash on the invoice before confirming, and check that hash's final status on the next tick before submitting anything new.

**Acceptance:** a test drives submit → timeout → later success and ends with exactly one settled invoice.

title: Make the confirm timeout and poll interval configurable
body:
`confirm()` polls every 1000ms with a fixed deadline. Move both into `SorobanExecutorConfig` with the current values as defaults.

**Acceptance:** a test with a 10ms poll interval no longer takes a second.

title: Resolve the token contract per asset instead of a single env var
body:
`tokenContractFor` is wired to one env var, so a deployment can only bill one asset. Store the SEP-41 contract id alongside the asset on the plan, and validate it at plan creation.

**Acceptance:** two plans in different assets bill correctly in one cycle.

title: Add plan upgrade and downgrade endpoints
body:
`prorate()` is implemented and tested but nothing calls it. Add `POST /v1/subscriptions/:id/change_plan` that prorates the current period, raises an adjustment invoice when something is owed, and moves the subscription to the new plan.

**Acceptance:** upgrade mid-period charges the difference; downgrade charges nothing and takes effect at the period boundary.

title: Accept idempotency keys on write endpoints
body:
A merchant retrying `POST /v1/subscriptions` after a timeout creates two subscriptions. Accept an `Idempotency-Key` header, store the first response for 24 hours, and replay it.

**Acceptance:** the same key returns the identical body and status; a different body under the same key is a 409.

title: Back API keys with hashed storage and rotation
body:
`RECUR_API_KEYS` is a comma-separated env var in plaintext. Add a merchant + api_key model, store only a hash, support two live keys per merchant so rotation has no downtime.

**Acceptance:** the env var path still works for local dev but logs a warning; auth is a constant-time hash comparison.

title: Generate an OpenAPI document from the Zod schemas
body:
The schemas in `packages/core/src/schema.ts` already describe every request body. Emit an OpenAPI 3.1 document from them and serve it at `/openapi.json`.

**Acceptance:** the document validates, and CI fails if it drifts from the committed copy.

title: Add rate limiting per API key
body:
No limits today. Add a token bucket per key, returning 429 with `Retry-After`.

**Acceptance:** limits are configurable; a test proves the bucket refills.

title: Return a consistent error envelope with a request id
body:
Errors are a mix of `{error}` and `{error, message}` and `{error, issues}`. Standardise on `{error, message, request_id, issues?}` and attach the request id to every response header.

**Acceptance:** every error path in `server.test.ts` asserts the shape.

title: Validate that a plan's asset issuer exists on the network
body:
A plan can be created with a well-formed but non-existent issuer, and only fails months later at charge time. Check the issuer account exists when the plan is created.

**Acceptance:** validation is skipped when no RPC URL is configured, so offline tests still pass.

title: Add a subscriptions list endpoint with status filtering
body:
There is no way to list subscriptions, only to fetch one by id. Add `GET /v1/subscriptions?status=past_due`.

**Acceptance:** filtered by the calling merchant, paginated, tested for cross-merchant leakage.

title: Add a pause and resume endpoint
body:
Merchants need to suspend billing without losing the subscription. Add a `paused` status that `due()` excludes, and endpoints to enter and leave it. Decide and document whether the period end shifts by the paused duration.

**Acceptance:** a paused subscription is never charged; resuming does not retroactively bill the paused periods.

title: Expose the payer's allowance state on the subscription resource
body:
A merchant cannot tell whether the next charge will succeed. Add `allowance_remaining` and `periods_covered` to the serialised subscription, read through the executor.

**Acceptance:** the field is null rather than an error when no network is configured.

title: Make webhook delivery durable with an outbox
body:
`deliver()` runs in-process; a crash loses the event. Persist a delivery row per (event, endpoint) with attempt count and next attempt time, and drain it from the scheduler tick.

**Acceptance:** killing the process mid-delivery still results in delivery after restart.

title: Add a webhook delivery log endpoint
body:
Merchants debugging an integration cannot see what we sent. Add `GET /v1/webhooks/:id/attempts` with status code, timestamp and attempt number — never the payload body, which may contain payer accounts.

**Acceptance:** paginated and scoped to the calling merchant.

title: Add a manual redelivery endpoint
body:
`POST /v1/events/:id/redeliver` to re-send one event to the endpoints subscribed to it.

**Acceptance:** redelivery is rate limited and recorded as a new attempt, not an edit of the old one.

title: Disable an endpoint after sustained failure and tell the merchant
body:
An endpoint that has failed every delivery for seven days should be marked inactive rather than retried forever.

**Acceptance:** documented threshold, an event when it happens, and a way to re-enable.

title: Publish a webhook verification snippet for other languages
body:
`verify()` exists in TypeScript only. Add tested equivalents in Python, Go and PHP to `docs/webhooks.md`.

**Acceptance:** each snippet verifies a fixture payload generated by the TypeScript implementation.

title: Add structured logging with pino across the API
body:
The API logs nothing and `main.ts` uses `console`. Wire pino into Fastify with request ids, and redact API keys and secrets in the serialisers.

**Acceptance:** a test asserts that a request carrying `x-api-key` never logs the key.

title: Add a /metrics endpoint
body:
Expose Prometheus metrics: charges attempted / succeeded / failed by failure code, cycle duration, due-queue depth, webhook delivery outcomes.

**Acceptance:** metrics are on a separate port or behind auth, never on the public API surface.

title: Add a readiness probe distinct from liveness
body:
`/health` returns ok before storage or RPC has been checked. Add `/ready` that verifies the store and, when configured, the RPC endpoint.

**Acceptance:** Dockerfile healthcheck points at the right one.

title: Emit a warning when a billing cycle overruns the tick interval
body:
If a cycle takes longer than `RECUR_TICK_INTERVAL_MS` the loops overlap silently. Measure the cycle and log a warning when it exceeds the interval; skip the next tick if one is still running.

**Acceptance:** covered by a test with a deliberately slow executor.

title: Add graceful shutdown to the API
body:
SIGTERM kills in-flight requests. Close the Fastify server, wait for in-flight work up to a timeout, then exit.

**Acceptance:** a request in flight during SIGTERM completes.

title: Write docs/quickstart.md: zero to first charge on testnet
body:
A single page taking a reader from `git clone` to a settled testnet charge, including funding accounts with friendbot and granting the allowance.

**Acceptance:** someone who has never used Stellar can follow it without opening another tab, and it is verified by running it.

title: Document the failure codes and what a merchant should do about each
body:
`FailureCode` has eight values with no user-facing documentation. Add a table to `docs/failures.md`: code, what it means, whether it retries, what the merchant should tell the payer.

**Acceptance:** linked from the README and from ADR 0004.

title: Add a sequence diagram of a full billing cycle
body:
ARCHITECTURE.md describes the cycle in prose. Add a Mermaid sequence diagram covering the success path and the retry path.

**Acceptance:** renders on GitHub; no detail in the diagram contradicts the code.

title: Add a worked example merchant integration
body:
Add `examples/merchant/` — a ~100-line Express app that creates a plan, subscribes a payer, receives webhooks with signature verification, and gates a route on subscription status.

**Acceptance:** runs against a local Recur with the mock executor, with its own README.

title: Publish a TypeScript client SDK
body:
Add `packages/client` — a typed wrapper over the REST API generated from or shared with the Zod schemas, with the webhook verifier included.

**Acceptance:** the example merchant app uses the SDK rather than raw fetch.

title: Set up eslint with a rule banning float arithmetic on amounts
body:
`pnpm lint` is declared but no eslint config exists. Add a flat config, and a custom rule (or a `no-restricted-syntax` pattern) that rejects `parseFloat`, `Number(` and `toFixed` inside `packages/core` and `packages/ledger`.

**Acceptance:** CI runs lint; the rule catches a deliberately added violation in a test fixture.

title: Add a changeset-based release flow for the published packages
body:
`@recur/core`, `@recur/ledger` and `@recur/stellar` are publishable but have no versioning story. Add changesets and a release workflow gated on CI.

**Acceptance:** a dry-run publish succeeds in CI without a token.

title: Add property-based tests for billing period arithmetic
body:
`advance()` has example-based tests. Add fast-check properties: advancing N times equals advancing by N; a period never has zero or negative length; a day-of-month anchor is preserved whenever the target month is long enough.

**Acceptance:** properties run in CI with a fixed seed and a documented budget.

title: Add a fuzz test for amount parsing
body:
`parseAmount` is the boundary between merchant input and money. Fuzz it: every input either throws or round-trips exactly through `formatAmount`.

**Acceptance:** no input produces a value that fails to round-trip.

title: Raise test coverage reporting and add a floor
body:
Coverage is configured but not reported or enforced. Publish the lcov report from CI and fail below an agreed line threshold for `packages/core` and `packages/ledger`.

**Acceptance:** the threshold is met by the current suite without weakening any test.

title: Add a load test for the billing cycle
body:
Seed 100k subscriptions in Postgres with 10k due in one tick, and measure the cycle. Record the numbers in `docs/performance.md`.

**Acceptance:** the run is scripted and repeatable, and identifies the dominant cost rather than just reporting a total.
